# Note: doc_trees does not include the "comm/" prefix to paths
# Note: In order for CI to pick up the need to rebuild docs, documentation
#  paths must include a "docs/" directory.
doc_trees:
    adr: docs/adr
    addrbook: mail/components/addrbook/docs
    backend: mailnews/base/docs
    build: docs/build
    calendar: calendar/docs
    cxx: docs/cxx
    documentation: docs/docs
    exchange: mailnews/protocols/exchange/docs
    frontend: mail/base/docs
    inappnotifications: mail/components/inappnotifications/docs
    l10n: docs/l10n
    mots: docs/mots
    panorama: mailnews/db/panorama/docs
    rust: rust/docs
    storybook: mail/components/storybook/docs
    telemetry: docs/telemetry
    testing: docs/testing

python_package_dirs: []

def __init__(self, topcommdir, main_path):
        self.topcommdir = topcommdir
        self.conf_py_path = os.path.join(main_path, "conf.py")
        self.index_path = os.path.join(main_path, "index.rst")

        with open(os.path.join(MAIN_DOC_PATH, "config.yml"), "r") as fh:
            self.config = yaml.safe_load(fh)

        self.trees = self.config["doc_trees"]
        self.python_package_dirs = self.config["python_package_dirs"]

text: 942 moves Rust documentation to rust/docs, and 943 stages document trees from docs/config.yml instead of extracting them from moz.build. The commit explains that Read the Docs has only Comm source. The accepted manager reads doc_trees and python_package_dirs from that configuration. Keep component documentation discovery in this explicit mapping so standalone source documentation does not require a Gecko checkout.
title: Register source documentation trees without depending on Gecko moz.build parsing
